title: Supply-curve token-econ allocations (hosted API)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a supply-curve approach for allocating hosted-API capacity and producing region+model-level token COGS slices. Use this to drive routing heuristics, reserve sizing, and short-run SKU pricing choices. This is an iterative workbook (not final)—aim is to land on defensible heuristics we can turn into routing knobs in the next sprint.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Problem: Per-token COGS varies nonlinearly with utilization and model family. Current flat regional heuristics miss tail effects and lead to margin leakage during bursts.
- Proposal: Build a supply curve per model-family+region that maps incremental token volume to marginal COGS. Use piecewise allocations for routing and a simple hysteresis band for short-term overflow.
- Outcome: Expected ~6-12% improvement in hosted-margin on mid-tail traffic by shifting 10-20% of burst volume to cheaper model-regions and enabling targeted reserve allocations.

Assumptions and data sources:
- GPU amortization, license, and infra egress are included in COGS.
- Metrics ingested from tokenflow-sheet (sheet:1A2b3CtokenEconSheetID) and regional-ppk logs (hourly sampling).
- Model families grouped: small-quick (Llama-7B-ish), mid (Llama-13B / mix), large (Llama-70B / LLMx).
- Time horizon for marginal slices: 1 hour (preferred) and 24 hour (for reserve sizing).
- Drop-in fallback model variants available (quantized / fewer layers) with known quality deltas.

Recommended spreadsheet structure (tabs):
- raw-inputs: hourly token volumes by model, region, slot utilization, price per GPU-hour, license amortization, egress cost.
- supply-curve: computed marginal COGS rows (see sample table below).
- routing-sim: simple simulator that applies allocation rules and computes per-token margin + SLA loss.
- scenarios: conservative / baseline / aggressive with knobs.
- actions: prioritized playbook and experiments.

SAMPLE: supply-curve (snippet, each row is a volume bucket ordered by increasing marginal cost)
Columns: bucket_id | cumulative_tokens_per_hr | marginal_ppk_usd | model_family | region | notes
1 | 0 - 50k | 0.00045 | small-quick | us-west-2 | reserved, high-efficiency slots
2 | 50k - 200k | 0.00072 | small-quick | us-west-2 | ondemand spill to smaller pods
3 | 200k - 500k | 0.00110 | mid | us-east-1 | requires mid-GPU with slightly higher license cost
4 | 500k - 800k | 0.00195 | large | eu-west-1 | overspill to larger instances + cross-region egress
5 | 800k+ | 0.00340 | fallback-quant | any | spot mix, degraded quality fallback

Key heuristics for routing: (to be implemented as step function knobs)
1) Target-first: route to lowest marginal_ppk bucket that meets latency target.
2) Spill-with-hysteresis: only spill if target bucket has sustained utilization > 80% for >= 5 minutes to avoid oscillation.
3) Quality-budget: track per-customer quality budget; if applying fallback-quant reduces eval score > threshold, cap fallback volume.
4) Reserve buffer: maintain per-region short-run reserve equal to 5th-95th percentile delta of hourly demand from previous 7 days (translated to token buckets).

Scenarios (quick simulation results from proto-sheet):
- Baseline: current routing (local-first), hosted margin = 36.2%, p50 latency = 140ms
- Supply-curve conservative: apply only bucket swaps when marginal delta >= 25% and sustained >10min. Hosted margin = 38.1%, p50 latency = 145ms (SLA unchanged)
- Supply-curve aggressive: allow cross-region spill for marginal delta >= 10% with 5min hysteresis. Hosted margin = 41.0%, p50 latency = 160ms (small SLA degradation for tail)
- Fallback-enabled: allow quantized fallback for non-PII workloads up to 12% of volume => additional 3.2% margin lift but requires eval-run.

Sensitivity notes (what changed margins):
- GPU price +15% -> margin delta: -4.8 percentage points for baseline; supply-curve aggressive mitigates to -3.0pp.
- Egress +10% -> cross-region moves become less attractive; recommended adjust spill threshold by +8pp.

Quality and risk controls (must ship before routing changes):
- Eval set: define 300 seed prompts (per customer segment) and measure quality delta vs. baseline model; require monitoring alert if regression > 2% on any slice.
- Audit logs: record routing decision, model_variant_id, and marginal_ppk at time of decision for post-hoc analysis.
- Opt-out: enterprise customers can opt out of cross-region or fallback.

Implementation notes for product-engineering:
- API: add optional routing_hint header that specifies "economy:low-cost" or "economy:balanced" to seed routing choices.
- Console: expose a per-route slider for spill sensitivity (0-100) and a toggle for fallback-quant.
- Backend: supply-curve lookup service returns next N candidate buckets with marginal_ppk and expected added latency.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How to price the quality delta? We can attach an internal "quality tax" in ppk that makes fallback less attractive, but need product buy-in.
- Reserve policy granularity: per-customer vs. per-region? Per-customer is fairer but operationally heavier.
- Billing implications for customers when we route cross-region for cost reasons (e.g., data residency).

Immediate next steps (owner + ETA):
- Aisha: canonicalize raw-inputs tab and publish to sheet (by 2024-11-15)
- Marco: implement supply-curve generator (prototype code + data pipeline) and push PR (git:github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pulls/xx) by 2024-11-25
- Evelyn: run 2-day eval jobs to surface quality regressions for fallback variants (by 2024-11-22)
- Jinsoo: sketch console UX for spill slider and routing summary (by 2024-11-20)

Meeting agenda for next sync (30m):
- Quick review of raw-inputs sanity checks (5m)
- Walkthrough of sample supply-curve and scenario sim (10m)
- Decide spill threshold defaults and hysteresis (10m)
- Assign infra tickets for supply-curve lookup service (5m)

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add per-model cold-start penalty to marginal_ppk in supply-curve (we currently underestimate for infrequent models)
- Reconcile spot-availability volatility: add a volatility multiplier in the scenarios tab
- Track customer complaints tied to cross-region routing in the first 2 weeks after rollout

End of doc.
